claims.quote: On the mantel, close to the gilt clock, a faint smear of oil caught the light when I put my palm over it — clock oil, dark and slightly sicced — and beside the clock there was an empty seat where a screw should have been. "The mantel clock, a gilt 19th-century piece, chimes every quarter-hour; its mechanism was Victor's pride." The bezel had a clear gap: a missing bezel screw.

There were other, smaller things. A faint grease smear along the mantel's edge where someone had rested a hand while fiddling with the clock; small metal filings gathered in the shadow beneath the gilt work; a tiny abrasion on the chair frame close to that worn circular spot, and one tuft of the upholstery pulled and stuck up as if fingers had worried at it.

I will be clear about a choice I made for the sake of being able to stage what followed: I found the obj-file-rasp in a top drawer of the loc-kitchen during my walk-through. The rasp had fresh filings in its teeth. I mark that location as my deliberate staging choice because the index did not specify where the rasp was found.

Lucy answered in short, trembling sentences. She could not hide how thin her voice had gone: "I— I was in the drawing-room. I heard the bell. I went to the study when Alfred called."

Alfred, when it came to his turn, gave a precise account of what he had been doing in the kitchen and when. He laid out his minutes like a clerk: he had lit the samovar, checked the oven at half-past eight, polished a tray at a quarter to nine and moved to fetch tea at nine.
The evidence made him the obvious suspect: the missing bezel screw, the fresh filings, his skill with small mechanisms.
I left the kitchen with that sentence under my tongue and the rasp in a paper towel at my hip.
